title: Transfer a section factor through a localized subalgebra inclusion
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, B an A-algebra, I an ideal of A, and sigma:B to A/I an A-algebra homomorphism. Suppose C0 is a commutative ring and e:B/IB to (A/I) times C0 is a ring isomorphism with first projection sigma. Let D be an A-subalgebra of B and b in D have idempotent image delta in D/ID. Suppose the canonical localization map D[1/b] to B[1/b] is bijective [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and e sends the image of b to (1,0). There exist an A/I-algebra C in the universe of B and a ring isomorphism Phi:D/ID to (A/I) times C respecting the A/I structure maps, sending delta to (1,0), with first projection sigma restricted to D.

source.place: Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5) implies (2), construction and closed-fibre decomposition of B''; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XI, read 2026-10-12

proof.text: Restrict sigma to D. It kills ID, so factor through a section s:D/ID to A/I; s(delta)=1. The localized algebra equivalence preserves the extended ideal I, and induces a quotient ring equivalence kq.

Quotient commutes with localization: the two localized quotients are localizations of D/ID and B/IB at the corresponding images of b. The induced quotient inclusion j and localization maps tD,tB satisfy kq(tD(x))=tB(j(x)).

If s(x)=s(y), applying e shows j(delta)*j(x)=j(delta)*j(y). Thus tB(j(x))=tB(j(y)), whence tD(x)=tD(y) by kq injectivity. The fraction equality criterion gives delta^n*x=delta^n*y. If n=0 multiply by delta; if n is positive idempotence gives delta*x=delta*y. Conversely the latter equality gives s(x)=s(y) because s(delta)=1.

Take C to be the (1-delta)-corner of D/ID, with the algebra map r sent to (1-delta) times its scalar image. Define Phi(x)=(s(x),(1-delta)*x). Injectivity follows from the preceding equality criterion and x=delta*x+(1-delta)*x. Surjectivity sends (r,y) to delta*algebraMap(r)+y: corner membership gives (1-delta)*y=y, hence s(y)=0. Scalar compatibility and Phi(delta)=(1,0) follow directly. The corner has the universe of D, which is the universe of B.

proof_origin.note: Explicit Lean realization of the finite-subalgebra and corner argument of Stacks 09XI.

lean.statement:
theorem quotient_section_factor_transfer
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (σ : B →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I)
    (C₀ : Type w) [CommRing C₀]
    (e : (B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃+* ((A ⧸ I) × C₀))
    (hes : ∀ x : B, (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x)).1 = σ x)
    (D : Subalgebra A B) (b : D)
    (hb : IsIdempotentElem (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A D)) b))
    (hloc : Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap D.val.toRingHom b))
    (heb : e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b.1) = (1, 0)) :
    ∃ (C : Type v) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra (A ⧸ I) C)
      (Φ : (D ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A D)) ≃+* ((A ⧸ I) × C)),
      (∀ a : A, Φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A D a)) =
        (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) (A ⧸ I) (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a),
          algebraMap (A ⧸ I) C (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a))) ∧
      Φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b) = (1, 0) ∧
      (∀ x : D, (Φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x)).1 = σ x.1)
